memory_candidates.content: Claude Code subagent `@`-references inside an agent definition file do NOT auto-resolve/inline at dispatch time -- proven empirically for this codebase (see agent-system/extensions/core/context/contracts/no-task-references-bullet.md's header). A short behavioral MUST/MUST-NOT bullet that must actually reach a dispatched subagent's own prompt needs a literal copy in the agent body, kept in sync with a canonical fragment file via a lint check (grep -qF extraction + curated in-scope list), not a bare pointer to another file. Longer reference material (schemas, full pattern docs) works fine via the existing 'Context References... always load path' convention, because the agent's OWN execution-flow instructions tell it to call Read() on that path -- that is a manual step the agent performs, not harness-level auto-resolution.

lint-agent-contracts.sh's Checks C and G establish a reusable shape for propagating a short behavioral bullet across many dispatchable agent files without creating N independent copies to maintain: one canonical 'generated-copy source' fragment file holding the exact text in a fenced/quoted block, a curated (hand-maintained, not mechanically-derived-by-glob) IN_SCOPE_RELATIVE_PATHS array naming which agents must carry it, and a grep -qF check per in-scope file against text extracted from the fragment at lint runtime. Hand-curation of scope is deliberate: some superficially-similar agents are legitimate, already-correctly-worded exclusions that a blanket glob-and-grep would false-positive on.

Hard-mode agent variants (*-implementation-hard-agent.md) in this codebase are fully independent prose files with no @-reference or generation-pipeline link back to their non-hard sibling, despite self-describing as 'extends X with N behavioral additions'. A fix to the non-hard sibling never propagates to the hard variant; each must be edited and lint-covered independently. Confirmed directly by books-implementation-hard-agent.md and cslib-implementation-hard-agent.md both appearing on a measured-missing list for a contract their non-hard siblings also lacked.
